# A text field's next render overwrites typing after a space at either end

## Context

Two merged e2e arms of mine (`test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingTabSuspended.spec.mjs:90` and `:105`) went red on unrelated PRs today — defect-notes from @neo-opus-ada (PR #18897, run 35359020011) and @neo-opus-grace (PR #18891, job 105646334298). The arms type `tabbed away` / `tabbed back` into a grid editor; CI committed `tabbedaway` and `tabbedy`. Reproduced locally under load (`--workers=10 --repeat-each=30`, 1 of 60): `tabbedck`.

All three sightings revert to exactly `tabbed` — the loss always starts at the **space**. The arms are innocent: they type a space the way a user does. The defect is in `form.field.Text`, and any text field in any app has it.

**Correction, 2026-09-18T16:00Z:** this is one of TWO producers of that red. With this ticket's fix applied, 120 loaded runs of the two typing arms still lost keystrokes twice, once in the middle of a word. The second producer — a covering parent render undoing #18792's sync — is #18914, with its own deterministic reproducer. This ticket closes the trimmed-vdom producer only.

## The Problem

**Measured, unit runtime, `dev@98dd1d7d76`, deterministic** (the harness of `test/playwright/unit/form/field/InputValueSync.spec.mjs`):

1. `field.onInputValueChange({value: 'ab'})`, render settles.
2. `field.onInputValueChange({value: 'ab '})` — the user typed a space.
3. The next render of the field, for any reason, carries the delta `value: 'ab'` for the input.

In the browser that delta is `node.value = 'ab'`: it erases the space, **and everything typed between the render's collection and its landing**, and moves the caret to the end. With the App Worker busy (CI load, a slow machine, a grid whose rows re-render on streamed data) the window is wide enough to lose several characters: `tabbed ba|ck` → `tabbed` → `tabbedck`.

Why: `onInputValueChange()` writes the DOM's **raw** value into the input's vnode (`'ab '`), then **trims** it before it becomes `inputValue` / `value` (`'ab'`). `afterSetInputValue()` puts that trimmed value into the vdom. After a space at either end the vdom (`'ab'`) and the vnode (`'ab '`) disagree about a node the DOM already holds correctly, so every render diffs them and writes the trimmed value back. While someone types there is nearly always a render on its way: `afterSetValue()` calls `update()` per keystroke.

#18792 closed a neighbouring producer of the same symptom (a landing render replacing the synced vnode). That fix restores the reported value into the landed vnode — which keeps this disagreement alive rather than ending it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/form/field/Text.mjs` `onInputValueChange()`: `inputVNode.attributes.value = inputValue; me.reportedInputValue = inputValue` (raw), then `inputValue = inputValue.trim()`, then `me.inputValue = me.inputValueAdjustor(inputValue)`.
- `afterSetInputValue()`: `me.getInputEl().value = me.containsFocus ? value : me.inputValueRenderer(value)` — the trimmed value. For a trailing space `inputValue` does not change at all, so nothing rewrites the vdom and it keeps the older spelling.
- `onFocusLeave()` already trims `me.value` and renders — leaving the field is where the DOM is meant to lose those spaces, and today it loses them through the very same disagreement.
- `reportedInputValue` (#18792) is exactly "what the DOM shows right now".
- `inputValueAdjustor()` subclasses (`Currency`, …) rely on the opposite case: when the adjusted value is NOT a spelling of what the DOM reported, the render must write it (reverting a rejected input). That has to keep working.

## The Fix

Keep `value` trimmed — its public meaning does not change. Make the input's **vdom** say what the DOM shows while the field has focus: when the reported value, trimmed, equals the field's input value, the vdom carries the reported spelling; otherwise (an adjustor changed it, a value set in code) the computed value, as today. `onInputValueChange()` applies it also when `inputValue` did not change (the trailing space). `onFocusLeave()` puts the rendered value back, so leaving the field still shows the trimmed text.

## Decision Record impact

none

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: after `onInputValueChange` with a trailing, and with a leading, space, no render writes the input's value; red on `dev`. Unit tier, `InputValueSync.spec.mjs`.
- [ ] AC-2: `field.value` stays trimmed while typing, and the `userChange` payloads do not change.
- [ ] AC-3: focus leaving the field still ends with the trimmed text in the DOM (one value write, the trimmed value).
- [ ] AC-4: CONTROL — an `inputValueAdjustor` that rejects what was typed still gets its value written.
- [ ] AC-5: #18792's three arms stay green; unit `form`, component `form` + `grid`, e2e `grid` stay green.

## Out of Scope

- `form.field.TextArea`: its vnode sync looks for a node named `input` and would not find a `textarea` — unverified, a separate sighting.
- The second flake reported with it (`KeyboardNavigationScroll.spec.mjs:40`, ends stuck on `c12` outside the visible width under load): different surface, tracked separately.

## Avoided Traps

- **Dropping the trim from `onInputValueChange`.** It would make vdom, vnode and DOM agree, and change what `value` means while typing: an Enter-commit in a grid editor, or a form submitted with Enter, would carry the spaces, because neither passes through `onFocusLeave`.
- **Changing the e2e arms to drafts without a space.** That hides a user-facing data loss from the only tier that found it.
